notes: The article unit on הַגּוֹיִם is correctly assigned, but its note misdescribes the placement: in 'O King of the nations' the written 'the' stands directly before 'nations', its own word, so nothing is fronted here — this is rule 29's ordinary case, not the fronting case. The same holds for חַכְמֵי הַגּוֹיִם, where the ASV writes a 'the' for each word and the construct takes a supplied one.
'royal estate' is headed on 'royal' by rule 31's subtraction; heading it on the noun 'estate' is the alternative and is rejected for the same reason 'dry land' heads on 'dry'.
מִי has an English word of its own, so under rule 17's second limit the fronted 'should' stays with the verb rather than going to an interrogative particle.
